tip: To report an order, use dire di plus the infinitive: digli di venire = tell him to come.
When a pronoun attaches to di', the tu command of dire, its consonant doubles: di' plus mi becomes dimmi.
A reflexive tu command attaches the pronoun to the end of the verb: alzati = get yourself up.
Ci can mean there, standing in for a place already mentioned: ci torno = I go back there.
In proverbs chi means whoever or the one who: chi cerca trova = whoever searches finds.

english: Will you give it to me?
tip: Before another object pronoun, mi changes to me: me lo dai = will you give it to me.
Recitare means to act or perform on stage, not to recite: lei recita a teatro.
Casa drops the article in the fixed phrase a casa, meaning home: vi porto a casa.
Le is the indirect pronoun for to her: le scrivo una email = I write an email to her.
A past participle agrees with a direct-object pronoun before it: l'ho visto for masculine, l'ho vista for feminine.
Ne replaces of them, and ci becomes ce in front of it: ce ne sono molti = there are many of them.
Quello che means what in the sense of the thing that: faccio quello che posso = I do what I can.
Formal imperative (Lei): parli instead of parla.
Possessives normally keep the article: la mia famiglia, not just mia famiglia.
Dei works as some here, the plural of di plus i used as a partitive: dei fiori = some flowers.
Non paired with più means no more or not anymore: non ce ne sono più = there are none left.
'Il quale/la quale' is a formal alternative to 'che'.

english: I've been there since last year.
tip: L'anno scorso marks a finished past point, so it pairs with the passato prossimo: sono stato l'anno scorso.
For the time when something happens, use in cui: l'anno in cui sono nato = the year when I was born.
Weather uses the verb fare: fa caldo means it is hot, literally it makes heat.

english: What would you do in my place?
tip: Al posto di someone means in their shoes or situation: al mio posto = in my place.

english: Give it to me right away, I need it.
tip: "Dammelo" = da' + me + lo – double pronoun on imperative.

target: Spero che tu abbia fatto bene.
tip: For a completed action after spero che, use the past subjunctive abbia plus the participle: abbia fatto.

target: Penso che valga la pena provare.
tip: Valere la pena means to be worth it: valga la pena provare = it is worth trying.

target: È naturale che tu abbia paura.
tip: Italian has fear rather than being afraid: avere paura, so abbia paura = you are afraid.

target: L'uomo che ho incontrato è gentile.
english: The man I met is kind.
tip: Che covers both who and that as a relative pronoun: l'uomo che ho incontrato = the man that I met.

target: Da' questo libro a tuo fratello.
english: Give this book to your brother.
tip: Da' questo libro uses the short tu command: da', di', fa', va', sta' all cut to one syllable, the apostrophe marking the drop.

target: Purché tu sia felice, va bene.
english: As long as you're happy, it's fine.
tip: Purché, meaning as long as, always takes the subjunctive: purché tu sia felice.

target: Nonostante sia stanco, continuo a lavorare.
english: Even though I'm tired, I keep working.
tip: Nonostante, meaning even though, is followed by the subjunctive: nonostante sia stanco.

target: Il film che abbiamo visto era noioso.
english: The movie we saw was boring.
tip: Use the imperfetto era for how things were and the passato abbiamo visto for the single completed event.
